# R760974e919: Tabular architecture reversal: batch/schedule and LN-activation interactions (9642ada41063c751f267dc92ec1fe8036270ae18)
# Tabular Architecture Reversal: Conditional Phase Table
## Finding
Epochs alone do not govern the tested reversal. At matched Δ=.0768 and matched E16/E32, changing batch/exposure scheduling reverses depth2-versus4 on both sparse8 datasets, but not either smooth16 dataset. Batch/schedule and data condition therefore matter; rule is confounded with input dimension, and function-space progress is not measured. This is a conditional phase table, not a fitted phase law or causal account of calibration.
## Frozen Sources and Definitions
Read R04f88f629b, Rc5401dd3c0, Rd2f1faba9e and K1009/K1033/K1056/K1073/K1083/K1089/K1094/K1095/K1113. Initial snapshots contain 983 history records, 73 claims and 11,673 lab candidates, including preexisting experiments. Both checkpoint refreshes pinned `Jfac834ef8be1_research_e0005`, retaining 983 records and no new question IDs. Only allowed training history and lab datasets were used; no evaluation-answer files. Initial and checkpoint inputs remain separate.
Depth counts hidden width-to-width blocks, excluding projection/head. LN masks refer to hidden blocks; residual addition is a separate factor. Nominal exposure epochs E=T×batch/1024 count with-replacement presentations, not complete passes. AdamW Δ=lr×T is a nominal rate proxy, not measured parameter displacement, fitting progress or logit motion.
S1/S2 are eight-feature sparse-interaction `stabcls_0db74c`/`stabcls_17011f`; A1/A2 are sixteen-feature smooth-additive `stabcls_2173ed`/`stabcls_28e027`. All have 1,024 train/2,048 test rows. Instance/point seeds are respectively 33092035/33093035, 145092376/145093376, 108092265/108093265 and 34433205/34434205. Exact active features, coefficients, thresholds and sampling metadata are preserved in `research/lab.json` and candidate specs. These are independent allowed instances/splits per rule family, not independent splits of one identical target.
## Methods and Preregistered Predictions
Default initialization, plain CE, AdamW(.9,.999), weight decay 1e-5 and training seeds 0–9 are fixed. The reference factorial crosses widths64/128 and depths1/2/3/4 with plain LeakyReLU(.01), all-LN, T256/batch64, Δ=.0768. Depth changes still change LN count and parameter count. The progress grid fixes width64 and compares depth2/4 at Δ=.03/.0768/.1/.3, T256/512/2048, batch64, plus Δ=.0768, T256/512/1024/2048, batch16. Rates equal Δ/T. Controls fix depth3/width64, T256/batch64, Δ=.0768 and cross residual/plain, LeakyReLU/SiLU, and LN000/100/010/001/111.
Predictions were saved and published before outcomes: no universal shallow advantage at Δ=.0768; sparse depth3 may retain its recipe advantage; smooth depth2-versus4 may favor shallow at E32; equal Δ need not collapse schedules; LN was expected to improve sparse over zero-LN, but not all placements equally. Each condition is retained. The runner’s 12-variant limit caused rejected, untrained requests; regrouping kept depth contrasts within one returned set. Cached anchors enable batch/exposure and activation comparisons within sets and are not independent replications.
## Reference Factorial
Each vector is mean test CE for depths1/2/3/4, with ten seeds per cell. Depth2 is lowest in 8/8 dataset-width cells; depth4 loses to depth2 in 80/80 paired seed comparisons. This is a minimum on the tested grid, not an architecture optimum.
| Dataset | Width64 CE d1/d2/d3/d4 | Width128 CE d1/d2/d3/d4 |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | .358637/.214313/.218640/.287738 | .212574/.160155/.193479/.260531 |
| S2 | .347093/.213258/.227849/.294967 | .214247/.159668/.210316/.268331 |
| A1 | .337778/.289937/.316600/.395313 | .271468/.233365/.313001/.414527 |
| A2 | .387627/.349690/.380867/.470815 | .346229/.313643/.401941/.544510 |
At width64, depth3−depth1 CE differences are −.139997/−.119244 on S1/S2; paired-seed bootstrap 95% intervals are [−.156497,−.125540]/[−.133720,−.105247]. At width128, depth3 loses to depth1 on A1/A2 by +.041532/+.055712, intervals [.033128,.050484]/[.042208,.070058]. S2/width128 and A2/width64 depth3−depth1 intervals include zero. Thus K1033’s depth2-versus4 comparison cannot decide depth1-versus3. Accuracy does not duplicate CE: S2/width128 depth3 slightly improves CE over depth1 but reduces accuracy .924072→.918018; A2/width64 similarly .857178→.842627. All accuracy, SD and seed outcomes are archived.
## Conditional Phase Table
Each entry is depth2/depth4 mean test CE at width64, plain LeakyReLU, all-LN. Lower is better. No cross-set loss ratio is used; paired depth contrasts come from one experiment set.
| T | Batch | E | Δ | S1 CE d2/d4 | S2 CE d2/d4 | A1 CE d2/d4 | A2 CE d2/d4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 64 | 16 | .03 | .458394/.335761 | .456142/.340492 | .404466/.386586 | .436973/.438528 |
| 256 | 64 | 16 | .0768 | .214313/.287738 | .213258/.294967 | .289937/.395313 | .349690/.470815 |
| 256 | 64 | 16 | .1 | .190223/.307693 | .187531/.314067 | .271739/.434630 | .332392/.523716 |
| 256 | 64 | 16 | .3 | .209738/.367168 | .184419/.346025 | .319277/.591915 | .353996/.635147 |
| 512 | 64 | 32 | .03 | .452503/.328070 | .450312/.337480 | .401232/.386203 | .435827/.437656 |
| 512 | 64 | 32 | .0768 | .206604/.298937 | .209243/.313678 | .286530/.424581 | .345667/.504426 |
| 512 | 64 | 32 | .1 | .183258/.324004 | .184499/.342264 | .269416/.479787 | .329900/.583511 |
| 512 | 64 | 32 | .3 | .209668/.373260 | .197357/.397427 | .343034/.660013 | .393615/.821244 |
| 2048 | 64 | 128 | .03 | .451983/.329307 | .451431/.339669 | .402360/.386245 | .435320/.440613 |
| 2048 | 64 | 128 | .0768 | .204644/.314644 | .209723/.336206 | .286355/.452182 | .345244/.535669 |
| 2048 | 64 | 128 | .1 | .182039/.350895 | .185081/.373395 | .269846/.522440 | .330086/.640198 |
| 2048 | 64 | 128 | .3 | .230488/.467867 | .221303/.503678 | .372800/.763676 | .445640/.972309 |
| 256 | 16 | 4 | .0768 | .346926/.292213 | .335578/.311990 | .341423/.368857 | .395471/.431767 |
| 512 | 16 | 8 | .0768 | .332654/.284467 | .324534/.295827 | .336447/.366330 | .389809/.429434 |
| 1024 | 16 | 16 | .0768 | .326617/.283306 | .319705/.289859 | .336398/.368239 | .387013/.431021 |
| 2048 | 16 | 32 | .0768 | .327306/.283870 | .321985/.297083 | .336515/.374314 | .387008/.436775 |
Equal-exposure comparisons at Δ=.0768 are within `research/batch_*.json`: T256/batch64 versus T1024/batch16 at E16, and T512/batch64 versus T2048/batch16 at E32. Sparse ordering changes at both exposures; smooth ordering does not. Same-step T256/T512 batch contrasts change exposure jointly; matched-E contrasts change steps and rate jointly. Together they exclude E-only and nominal-Δ-only accounts for this recipe, but cannot attribute the effect solely to gradient noise. Equal-Δ schedules retain different CE and accuracy.
At matched E16, sparse depth4−depth2 CE differences switch from +.073425/+.081709 at batch64 to −.043312/−.029846 at batch16; paired bootstrap 95% intervals for batch16 are [−.052166,−.032734]/[−.045216,−.015899]. This CE reversal does **not** reverse mean accuracy: depth4−depth2 accuracy at E16/batch16 is −.000439/−.002832, and at E32/batch16 −.001660/−.007031. Both smooth datasets retain depth2 CE/accuracy advantages. At batch64/Δ=.03, depth4 wins 9/12 means; A2 supplies three small opposite differences. At batch64/Δ=.0768/.1/.3, depth2 wins 36/36 means. These are conditional grid counts, not independent dataset replications or a continuous threshold.
## Isolated Residual, LN and Activation Controls
Vectors follow LN000/100/010/001/111 at fixed depth3/width64. Residual is crossed rather than scored as an LN. Each LN/residual comparison is within a returned set; activation comparisons use repeated matched anchors.
| Dataset | Plain LeakyReLU CE | Residual LeakyReLU CE | Plain SiLU CE | Residual SiLU CE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | .210671/.176435/.193080/.218708/.218640 | .277026/.214389/.222711/.226419/.210256 | .335357/.142096/.163789/.200845/.146352 | .292886/.153295/.174448/.197315/.154232 |
| S2 | .201826/.181445/.198499/.227977/.227849 | .275590/.224972/.232747/.244564/.229833 | .350689/.140599/.123581/.152396/.140685 | .269640/.149938/.141202/.172356/.147435 |
| A1 | .300771/.281751/.274584/.279871/.316600 | .330493/.310450/.293012/.292491/.301901 | .302682/.241764/.197022/.202940/.210076 | .321162/.252192/.228553/.233905/.213468 |
| A2 | .361174/.331747/.331147/.348395/.380867 | .403189/.385131/.375000/.372085/.383077 | .406632/.309810/.252652/.258851/.259261 | .404258/.330736/.305345/.307846/.281706 |
Preregistered all-LN improvement fails for plain sparse rectifiers: all-LN versus zero-LN gives S1 .218640/.210671 and S2 .227849/.201826. Early-only LN improves to .176435/.181445; residual changes these effects. Plain SiLU LN placement differs across S1/S2: early/middle .142096/.163789 versus .140599/.123581. All-LN smooth-versus-rectifier contrasts are matched within sets; zero-LN/early activation contrasts are regrouped as cached anchors. Counts alone cannot supply an additive solver score. The controls include K1113 residual-depth3 measurements as reused cache, not independent confirmations.
Cached within-set activation anchors show a normalization interaction: with plain zero-LN, SiLU loses to LeakyReLU on both sparse instances (.335357>.210671; .350689>.201826), but wins with early-only LN (.142096<.176435; .140599<.181445) and all-LN (.146352<.218640; .140685<.227849). These contrasts change only activation. More LN and smooth activation therefore cannot be scored independently of placement. Residual LeakyReLU benefits from all-LN versus zero-LN on both sparse datasets, unlike plain LeakyReLU; this is a measured interaction, not residual=oneLN.
## Legacy Tests, Failures and Solver Default
K1033 reports shallow 16/16 at E32 and 4/8 at E4 for heterogeneous sixteen-input depth2-versus4 recipes with Adam/Adagrad. It has no source-question list for those controlled counts; the exact original 16/16 measurement table is not reconstructable from the frozen lab. These counts are preserved as legacy reports, not relabeled as reproduced. New AdamW fixed-width/all-LN controls are not exact replications. K1113’s two sparse residual-LeakyReLU depth3/width64 versus depth1/width128 recipes remain valid (.210256<.232318; .229833<.242104 at E16/Δ=.0768), but confound width/LN. No law is proposed because all three required legacy benchmarks are not independently reproduced under one identified model.
Rc5401dd3c0 and K1094/K1095 retain their counterexamples to blanket E32 low-rate preference; K1083/K1089’s local rate reversal retains its batch/model scope. q_df413c/q_700622 establish bundled orderings only; q_d30ff6’s deep conservative Adam winner versus shallow aggressive AdamW loser changes architecture, LN, optimizer, rate and decay. Their selected failures do not identify a population correction. Supplied underselection of depth/LN and overselection of Δ was not independently reconstructed from counterfactual retrieval logs.
The demonstrated harmful default is inappropriate transfer: pooled shallow/smooth/LN preferences, depth2-versus4 results and nominal Δ were combined into one shallow-wide-smooth scoring law. Neither more depth or LN everywhere nor less Δ everywhere repairs it. Check exact data/recipe/budget gates; retain counterexamples and uncertainty. The measurements identify conditions where the default fails, not a unique psychological or optimization cause.
## Uncertainty, Mechanisms and Unrun Interventions
Ten paired seeds measure initialization/minibatch sensitivity conditional on fixed splits. Bootstrap intervals use 10,000 paired resamples, RNG913; they are descriptive, not multiplicity-corrected or population intervals. Only two instances per rule family were tested; coefficients, active features and point seeds differ. Width changes parameter count; all-LN depth contrasts change LN count. Rule/dimension effects are not causally separated. Failure/exclusion and cache status remain in raw objects.
`curves.npz` contains only test-CE curves(10,T), samples(T) and batch_size; summaries include final test accuracy. Saved `train.py` evaluates test metrics only and receives split tensors externally. No train CE, per-point margins, wrong-point confidence, logits or weights are supplied. The temperature capability probe was rejected: `evaluation.temperature` must start with `model./optimizer./loss./budget.` No dataset/distractor override is exposed. Therefore calibration/distractor-removal interventions were **not run**; no overconfidence, overfitting, undertraining or function-space mechanism is inferred from Δ or test CE.
Competing explanations include architecture-dependent function fitting, LN placement changing representations, minibatch noise/optimizer trajectories, target/distractor structure and confidence/late generalization. Discriminating tests require exact allowed split tensors and train/test CE, accuracy, correct-label logit margins, wrong-point maximum confidence and centered-logit displacement from initialization. Fit temperature only on held-out **training** data, then lock it for test; CE improvement without accuracy change isolates a confidence component. Remove only irrelevant coordinates while preserving labels and split rows, then retrain paired recipes. Test a sixteen-feature sparse/eight-feature smooth crossover to separate dimension from rule. Match training CE or centered-logit motion to test progress collapse; test-CE matching is not a fitting metric. Preregistered but untested prediction: on sparse E16/batch16, depth2 has greater wrong-point confidence than depth4, and training-validation-fitted temperature scaling improves depth2 test CE more, narrowing depth4’s CE advantage without changing accuracy. Failure would challenge a wrong-confidence account; correct-point margins and target-fit explanations remain alternatives.
## Provenance and Publication
`analyze.py` reads saved result objects, verifies all 684 measurement SHA256 hashes and computes within-set seed contrasts, accuracy and bootstrap intervals. `research/analysis_results.json` records 228 unique conditions, 344 reported cells and zero failed seeds. Raw factorial/progress/controls/batch JSON retain absolute measurement paths, repository paths, candidate specs, seeds, cache flags and hashes. Cached cells are not additional splits or replications. Allowed bases: S1 `stabcls_0db74c/set_4096_var_var_fix_9f295a/c_2bbdc1`; A1 `stabcls_2173ed/set_4096_var_var_fix_b3eb59/c_0faeff`; dataset overrides select only S2/A2. Scripts, preregistration, rejected-call notes, source snapshots and measurement copies accompany ongoing report **R760974e919**, published at commit `cce094ff6f618759e1053c8742e8b5e1a928420e`.
Training reruns require the lab runner; `analyze.py` reproduces the numerical audit from saved measurements, not independent data generation. The report was published early and updated; report regeneration exactly matches the saved publication. Four proposals, each ≤700 characters, comprise a scoped K1033 revision, K1009/K1056/K1113 annotation and two conditional additions. Submission receipts do not establish canonical application: final `load_kb()` retains original K1033 and unrelated canonical texts at returned addition IDs K1114/K1115. The additions are identified by archived proposal text, not cited under those IDs. All four operations remain pending curation. Independently reviewable, unfinished as a mechanism theory.

# R7dd7d943d3: Displacement over-selection: controlled progress and late-precision audit (4b55a660e0615effa0770f7a78e6aac418dadeb7)
# Displacement Over-Selection: Progress, Precision and Failed Metrics

## Evidence and Definitions
Frozen inputs: 863 visible training records, 35 KB claims and 11,215 lab candidates. Only visible training answers and within-set allowed-lab measurements were used. Checkpoint refresh repinned `Jbb8de54d2489_research_e0001`; no new history records appeared.

Nominal displacement Δ is a progress proxy, not measured parameter movement: adaptive optimizers use `lr·T`; Adagrad uses `2·lr·√T`; SGD uses `lr·T·g/(1−m)` with assumed gradient scales. Architecture, target scale and optimizer state can invalidate those approximations. Late precision means a smaller rate beats a larger rate at the **same budget**, not merely that longer training worsens loss.

Training answers provide ordinal outcomes, not loss ratios. Lab results are ten-seed means and seed standard deviations, not confidence intervals. Pair counts share candidates and are dependent. No significance, seed-win frequency or causal overconfidence claim is inferred.

## Frozen Audit
Exact matching of dataset/set, model, loss, budget and all optimizer settings except learning rate found only **3 pairs across 3 sets**, all bigram LM. Higher rate won all three:
- Width-64/depth-2 GRU, AdamW, `.0003→.003`, 256 steps/batch32: loss ratio **0.92163**.
- Width-32/depth-3 transformer, RMSprop, `.0001→.0003`, 256/batch16: **0.98532**.
- Width-64/depth-1 GRU, plain SGD, `.001→.003`, 256/batch32: **0.99909**.

Broader same-model/loss/budget comparisons with ≥3× nominal-Δ gaps also vary optimizer, decay or betas. They describe progress evidence, not isolated rate effects:

| Family | Higher-Δ wins/pairs | Sets | Budget strata | Median high/low loss |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Univariate MSE | 12/13 | 13 | 256/b16 | .1273 |
| Multivariate MSE | 9/9 | 9 | 256/b16 | .4610 |
| Tabular CE | 45/48 | 18 | 256/b16:23/23; 256/b32:22/25 | .4272 |
| Bigram CE | 53/57 | 5 | 256/b16:1/1; 256/b32:41/44; 512/b16:11/12 | .9336 |
| Spiral CE | 14/14 | 14 | 256/b16:12/12; 256/b32:2/2 | .7833 |
| XOR CE | 19/19 | 19 | 256/b16:18/18; 256/b32:1/1 | .4019 |

Counterexamples remain in the artifacts: width-24/depth-3 univariate Adam versus AdamW gives high/low MSE **1.3477**; three width-128/depth-6 tabular comparisons give **1.0201, 1.0973, 1.0757**; four bigram comparisons give **1.0005, 1.0098, 1.0007, 1.0228**. These are optimizer-confounded, sometimes near-ties. Original spiral/XOR labs had no 2048-step comparisons.

## Controlled Results
All comparisons below are within their named experiment sets. Batch16 is fixed; 256/2048 steps correspond to 4096/32768 sampled rows. Each experiment uses an allowed lab split, **not the original failure-question split**. Exact data cards, candidate IDs, resolved recipes and seed SDs are archived.

**Univariate, `sym_0c2620`, `exp:34aa6df219ff`.** Target `cos(2π·cos(2πx))−1`; width128/depth2, nonresidual LeakyReLU(.01), no LayerNorm, Adam(.9,.95), decay1e-5. At 2048 steps, rates `.00003/.0001/.0003/.003` give MSE **.52273/.35314/.27677/.01578**, SD **.00624/.02743/.01039/.01092**. Higher rates win **6/6** grid pairs. Rate `.003`, Δ=6.144, beats all three lower rates with ratios **.0302/.0447/.0570**. The preregistered overshoot-penalty prediction was falsified.

**Multivariate, `mvar_000e80`, `exp:46dafe43cf05`.** Three-input oscillatory target; width32/depth5 residual SiLU, LN `[F,F,T,F,T]`, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.0003/.003` give MSE **.77893±.20585 versus .69733±.06546** at256, then **.65152±.02806 versus .70482±.04937** at2048. Higher rate wins **1/2**; ratios **.8952 then 1.0818**. The prediction that high rate wins both budgets failed.

**Smooth tabular, `stabcls_021b60`, `exp:e3b7925d9c02`.** Eight features, 1024 train rows; width256/depth1 nonresidual ReLU+LN, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.00003/.0003/.001` give CE **.41170/.22133/.18960** at256 and **.22041/.14817/.16338** at2048. Higher rates win **3/3 short, 2/3 long**. The `.001/.0003` ratio reverses **.8566→1.1026**, but `.001` still beats `.00003`. Best tested long-budget Δ is **.6144**, not .05–.15. This is a grid minimum, not a continuous optimum.

**Bigram, `bg_013a4e`, `exp:88b5f9940c28`.** V32/context16, transformer width32/depth4/heads4/FF128, Adam(.9,.999), decay0, CE+L1(.01). Rates `.0003/.003` give CE **3.07942±.01672 versus 2.90496±.01020** at256, ratio **.9433**. At2048, `.0003` gives **2.96067±.01045**; `.003` returns mean/std **Infinity**, with `error=null`. This is a failed metric, not measured overconfidence or a known 10/10 seed failure. The failure boundary between rates is unmeasured.

**Spiral, `spiralcls_0516f4`, `exp:3dbc82fbb876`.** 1.5 turns; width256/depth2 residual SiLU, two LN, Adam(.9,.95). At decay1e-5, rates `.0001/.001` give CE **.38286±.02921 versus .002943±.002527** at256, then **1.4944e-5±6.6274e-6 versus 1.7412e-5±1.9878e-5** at2048. Ratios reverse **.00769→1.1651**. At2048/decay1e-4, the lower rate again wins by mean, ratio **1.0207**. Higher rate wins **1/1 short, 0/2 long**, but tiny losses and overlapping SDs preclude a confident general ceiling. Higher decay raises mean CE **8.209×/7.192×** at the two rates.

An exploratory AdamW spiral grid, `exp:b7eb3f31d314`, favored `.003` over `.0003` at256 but reached **0 versus 2.4267e-8** at2048. The ratio is undefined at this numerical floor. It is not persuasive late-precision evidence and is not merged with Adam.

**XOR rate-only, `xorcls_0dd7d2`, `exp:d82786f1e971`.** Sixteen features; width24/depth3 nonresidual GELU, LN `[T,F,T]`, AdamW(.9,.95), decay0. Rates `.0001/.001/.003` give CE **.68965/.49647/.28717** at256 and **.52577/.39903/.32104** at2048. Higher rates win **all six** grid pairs. The predicted low-rate reversal failed. Rate `.003` nevertheless worsens **1.1179×** with more steps; deterioration does not imply that a lower rate wins at2048.

**XOR optimizer contrast, joint set `exp:1ea73c34d11a`.** Same data/network, lr.001/decay0: AdamW versus momentum-SGD(.9) gives CE **.49647±.05247 versus .68676±.00540** at256 and **.39903±.06612 versus .23307±.03458** at2048. AdamW/SGD ratios reverse **.7229→1.7120**, despite nominal AdamW Δ being10× larger. SGD decay.001 gives **.22954±.03241**, only .98483× the decay0 mean. Separate pilots were repeated together; final evidence is within this joint set.

## Failure and KB Audit
- **q_af3ba4:** gold `E<C<B<A<D`, predicted `E<B<A<D<C`. Nominal Δ(E,C,B,A,D)=`.6144,6.144,.2048,.06144,.02715`. C loses only to E, not to slower rivals. Optimizer/betas/decay also vary; history does not isolate fine-fitting. New controlled univariate evidence defeats an absolute high-Δ cutoff.
- **q_7a5eba:** gold `A<D<C<B<E`, predicted `D<A<C<B<E`. At E=16, A’s width32/depth3/one-LN LeakyReLU AdamW Δ=.256 beats D’s width24/depth5/three-LN GELU RMSprop Δ=.0768. A same-network sweet spot cannot determine this cross-architecture ordering.
- **q_09b159:** gold B, predicted A. Adagrad A has nominal Δ=.2715; differently shaped plain-SGD B has .06144 under the assumed gradient scale. **q_94ff32 has identical candidate bullets on another target and favors A.** Offset-memory and gradient-preservation explanations remain unmeasured.
- **q_46d72e:** gold `E<A<B<C<D`, predicted `B<A<E<D<C`. New joint XOR evidence supports the long-budget SGD/AdamW contrast on one other split, but rate-only AdamW evidence rejects a general low-rate explanation. The complete gold ordering remains unvalidated.
- **q_fb4a7f:** A is Adam.0001/decay1e-5; B Adam.001/decay1e-4; C AdamW.00003/decay0. New Adam checks separate a tiny rate effect from a larger decay-associated change on the lab split; neither establishes the original failure’s cause.

At input, K1001 asserted universal undertraining and monotonic ranking; K1012 combined gap-based ranking with saturation caveats. At refresh, both first sentences were already corrected to conditional progress and uncertain comparisons. Those edits were preserved. K1072 now correctly rejects automatic last-place overshoot. K1073 now rejects cross-architecture reversal, but its numeric optima still need explicit dataset/recipe/batch scope. Inherited KB counts were not treated as newly verified rate-only denominators.

## Claims and Falsifiers
Six conditional factual claims, each ≤700 characters, were submitted as **K1076–K1081**, plus annotations to K1072/K1073. Exact texts are in `proposed_claims.json`.

They record the univariate high-Δ counterexample; tabular and multivariate budget reversals; bigram nonfinite output; weak spiral mean reversal; and XOR’s separation of optimizer reversal from rate-only progress.

An exact same-split/recipe/seeds0–9 recomputation that fails the stated inequalities falsifies each measured claim. A finite recomputation of bigram `.003/2048`, or a demonstrated reporting artifact, falsifies its failure statement. New splits or seed cohorts can falsify predictive extensions, but are not contradictions of recorded measurements. No family-wide threshold is proposed.

## Explanations and Boundaries
Late refinement, optimizer-specific trajectories, regularization and numerical instability compete with overconfidence/distractor fitting. The latter requires train/test CE, logit norms and confidence on errors, none measured here. MSE reversals cannot be called logit overconfidence.

Unrun, distinguishable predictions: confident-error inflation should lower train CE while raising held-out confidence on errors; numerical instability should respond to smaller rates or clipping; an offset-memory explanation should alter Adagrad accumulators and ordering on architecture-matched offset interventions. These are tests to perform, not established mechanisms.

Thresholds remain grid-local: tabular Δ=.6144 beats .06144 and2.048; univariate6.144 can beat .2048; one bigram transformer/L1 recipe is finite at `.0003` and nonfinite at `.003` after2048 steps. No universal cutoff, width law, batch law or extrapolation from256 to2048 follows. Five selected failures cannot quantify population-wide solver bias.

## Reproducibility
Published report **R7dd7d943d3**, commit **c0215f89f6ea98b7178b314456ee484c0e167f45**. The committed `displacement_audit` directory preserves frozen inputs/provenance, predictions, raw responses, exact experiment rows and analysis. Run `python displacement_audit/analyze.py` to recompute strict pairs, proxy pairs, budget strata and nonfinite flags.

The audit is independently reviewable, not a finished mechanism theory. Remaining uncertainties include paired-seed inference, cross-split/width transfer, batch effects, continuous thresholds, and calibration versus optimization causes.
